candidate_relations.reason: Although the imaging shows classic AIP features (sausage-shaped pancreas, capsule-like rim, diffuse narrowing of MPD), the markedly elevated CEA (28.8 ng/mL), very high FDG-PET SUVmax (8.6 pancreas, 10.0 lymph nodes), new-onset diabetes (HbA1c 7.2%), and normal IgG4 collectively favor malignancy. The reference diagnosis is pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and AIP is a conflicting benign entity, not an alias.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: AIP is a key differential but is a distinct benign entity incompatible with the reference diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma

candidate_relations.label: Pancreatic Cancer
candidate_relations.reason: Pancreatic cancer is the conventional clinical shorthand for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. The clinical features—obstructive jaundice, elevated CEA, elevated CA19-9, diffuse FDG-avid pancreatic lesion with hypermetabolic lymph nodes, bile duct and pancreatic duct stenosis, and new-onset diabetes—are consistent with the reference diagnosis. The label is a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Pancreatic cancer is a standard alias for pancreatic adenocarcinoma, the reference diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Imaging features mimic autoimmune pancreatitis (type 1), creating a diagnostically challenging overlap; elevated CEA and high FDG SUVmax are the key discriminators favoring malignancy over AIP
Normal IgG4 and amylase reduce likelihood of AIP but do not exclude it entirely; tissue confirmation would be standard of care
